subject: Post-demo: model shortlist + benchmarks / next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Lee <dana.lee@acme.com>, Alex Martin <alex.martin@acme.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: model shortlist + benchmarks / next steps

Thanks again for the time this morning — really appreciated the walk-through of Acme's customer-support use case and the sample transcripts. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture a concise shortlist of models we recommend for the pilot, the tradeoffs, and proposed next steps. Attaching our benchmark CSV and the prompt set we used to run the demo (acme-prompt-set-v1.jsonl).

Recommended shortlist (prioritized for pilot):
1) Redwood-13B (int8 quantized) — recommended first pilot.
   - Rationale: Best balance of unit cost, throughput, and solid QA accuracy on conversational support prompts.
   - Observed: 95th-pct token latency ~65ms on our Dedicated config; median ~28ms. Best-in-class cost for chat workloads when paired with KV prefix caching.
   - Cost proxy: approx $7.50 per 1M input+output tokens on Dedicated (post-discount).

2) Falcon-40B (8-bit) — higher quality than 13B on long-context reasoning, moderate cost.
   - Rationale: Shows stronger multi-step reasoning and fewer instruction-following failures on your eval prompts; ~2x cost vs 13B.
   - Observed: 95th-pct token latency ~120ms; median ~55ms.

3) Llama2-70B (fp16) — highest quality fallback for edge cases.
   - Rationale: Best raw quality on fuzzy/ambiguous user asks; recommend as canary/fallback for critical flows where correctness is prioritized over cost.
   - Observed: 95th-pct token latency ~260ms; cost proxy ~4–5x Redwood-13B.

Notes / risks:
- Quantization: our int8 path for Redwood-13B shows small regression on a subset of hallucination-sensitive prompts — we flagged ~1.8% drop in answer-accuracy vs fp16. We recommend running the full Acme eval set to quantify impact.
- Prompt sensitivity: some multi-turn resolution prompts benefit from light prompt engineering (explicit step-by-step constraints) — we included a suggested prompt template in the attached JSONL.

Attachments: redwood-model-benchmarks-20260325.csv, acme-prompt-set-v1.jsonl

Next steps I propose:
- We run your canonical eval set (you can share a small holdout of ~500 pairs) against the three candidate models on Redwood Dedicated and produce a per-class breakdown (accuracy, F1, hallucination rate).
- 2-week pilot: Redwood-13B as primary, Falcon-40B for medium-difficulty queries; Llama2-70B as on-demand fallback for high-risk queries.
- We’ll include rollout instrumentation (A/B by user segment, confidence thresholding, and automatic fallback).

If that plan looks good I’ll coordinate with Connor to scope the eval run and share timing + costs.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0123

Appreciate the quick reply — and yes, please send the sanitized 500-example eval when ready. Quick notes and the granular numbers you asked for (summary here; full CSV attached):

Cost (ballpark, per-1M input+output tokens):
- Hosted API (on-demand):
  - Redwood-13B (int8): ~$18 / 1M tokens
  - Falcon-40B (8-bit): ~$38 / 1M tokens
  - Llama2-70B (fp16): ~$110 / 1M tokens
- Dedicated (reserved, committed throughput): approx 40–60% lower unit cost depending on commit level:
  - Redwood-13B (int8): ~$7.5 / 1M tokens
  - Falcon-40B (8-bit): ~$22 / 1M tokens
  - Llama2-70B (fp16): ~$45–70 / 1M tokens (depends on consolidation w/ other workloads)

Quality/Regression notes (from our internal eval on the demo prompt set — attached):
- Redwood-13B int8 vs fp16: ~1.8% absolute drop in answer-accuracy on hallucination-sensitive examples; most common failure mode is confident-but-incorrect short factuals.
- Falcon-40B (8-bit): tiny regression vs fp16 (~0.6%) but better baseline vs 13B on multi-step reconciliation prompts.
- Llama2-70B: baseline best quality; negligible regression when moving from fp16->8/4-bit (we generally avoid aggressive 4-bit quant on 70B for these flows).

We can run your 500-sample eval in either Dedicated or Private. Recommended path: Dedicated pilot (2 weeks) + share all outputs/logs and a short regression report. If privacy/compliance requires Private deployment we can run the same eval there (longer lead time for onboarding).

Proposed timing/cost for the eval run:
- Setup + scheduling: 2 business days
- Eval run (500 examples across 3 models, full token logging): 1 business day runtime
- Analysis + report: 2 business days
- Estimated one-time eval cost (compute + analysis): ~$2.5k on Dedicated for the set above (we’ll provide a formal quote once we confirm commit level).

I’ve also uploaded the raw benchmark CSV to a shared drive and linked the eval dashboard above. Let me know if you want a quick call tomorrow to align on tooling/access.

Best,
Marissa

(attachments: redwood-model-benchmarks-20260325.csv, acme-prompt-set-v1.jsonl)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Looping in a couple operational/rollout suggestions from an infra perspective. Quick notes:
- Rollout approach: start with a 10% traffic canary (Redwood-13B int8) + 10% on Falcon-40B for medium complexity; route anything flagged as high-risk (confidence < 0.6 or matching PO/invoice intents) to Llama2-70B.
- A/B experiment: keep a small holdout (5–10%) on fp16 vs int8 to continuously measure regression and drift. We recommend automatic rollback if hallucination-rate delta > 2.5% over a 48-hour window.
- Quantization policy: int8 for 13B is fine for production after the eval; for Falcon we recommend 8-bit with per-layer calibration. Avoid 4-bit on Llama2-70B for production-critical flows.
- Observability: enable per-request tagging and sample capture for low-confidence answers. We’ll provide a quality dashboard slice for your CS team.

Happy to help scope the routing rules and can share a sample canary config + A/B plan.

—Connor
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
